title: Beyond the AI Hype: The Operational Blueprint for Freight Forwarding Intelligence
body_markdown:
With over 25 years of global technology, digital trade, and supply chain leadership—including scaling Western tech enterprises across Asia and leading an e-commerce infrastructure startup to an Alibaba acquisition—Joyce Tai brings rare, front-row perspective to the realities of logistics digitalization. Today, as Executive Vice President of Worldwide Partnerships at Freightos, she collaborates directly with the world’s leading freight forwarders, carriers, and enterprise shippers navigating cross-border trade.


While generative AI and autonomous agents dominate industry headlines, the operational reality on the forwarding floor looks very different. Many forwarders attempting to automate quotations encounter wildly erratic rates, stalled pilots, and internal user resistance—not because the technology lacks capability, but because the foundational pricing data and organizational boundaries remain fragmented.


In this three-part edition of ***Freightos Thoughts*** , Joyce cuts through the AI noise to deliver a pragmatic roadmap for logistics leaders. Across three concise video breakdowns, she examines:


### The Inconsistent Rate Dilemma: Why Agentic AI Fails at Autonomous Quoting


- **The Inconsistent Rate Dilemma:** Forwarders testing agentic AI frequently encounter wildly erratic pricing results on identical trade lanes—such as two containers from Shanghai to the US—leading to frustration and mistrust in the technology.
- **Automating Operational Ambiguity:** AI models do not operate in a vacuum; when internal human workflows feature overlapping responsibilities and blurred operational boundaries, autonomous agents replicate that same confusion at scale.
- **The Non-Negotiable Data Foundation:** Inconsistent outputs stem directly from unstandardized buy/sell data, fragmented margins, and missing context. Without clean operational fuel, autonomous quoting engines cannot generate reliable answers.
- **The Reality of AI Readiness:** Deploying agents before codifying internal pricing logic and consolidating core rate data only amplifies operational noise rather than solving efficiency bottlenecks.


### Why Freight Forwarders Need Assisted Intelligence, Not Full Automation


- **Beyond Transactional Quoting:** Looking up rates, preparing a spreadsheet, and emailing a price isn’t strategic work; true forwarding value lies in consultative advisory and proactive risk mitigation.
- **Context-Driven Intelligence:** A fully enabled quoting workspace arms the specialist with historical customer sentiment, carrier service ratings, and real-time operational disruption alerts right at the moment of search.
- **Assisted Execution Over Human Replacement:** AI should not be built to eliminate industry talent, but to automate administrative baseline searches so professionals can advise shippers on transit tradeoffs, strike risks, and General Rate Increases (GRIs).


### The 4-Phase Digitization Roadmap: Why Phase 0 Forwarders Can’t Skip to AI


- **The Phase 0 Reality:** A significant portion of small-to-midsize forwarders operate in Phase 0—where critical buy rates, sell rates, and margin formulas live offline in spreadsheets or personal desktops.
- **The “Garbage In, Garbage Out” Trap:** Rushing into AI adoption without standardizing baseline pricing workflows inevitably leads to failed implementations and wasted capital.
- **Step-by-Step Digitization:** Forwarders must progress sequentially: centralizing rates into a common infrastructure before layering on automation or cognitive models.
- **Pragmatic Foundations First:** Sustainable tech adoption requires meeting logistics organizations at their actual maturity stage rather than pitching one-size-fits-all autonomous tools.
